title: What is ATTP, and what does membership of the Association give you?
excerpt: Information for anyone who wants to join our Association
body_html:
The National Association ATTP and its membership!

For those asking: “What does belonging to ATTP give me?”

Of course this question was bound to come up, especially as the situation in table tennis in the Republic of Moldova became uncertain and disagreements between sports clubs grew more pronounced. We could suggest studying the Association’s Statute, but to set aside time for that you would probably need to be quite deeply interested in the subject.

ATTP’s Statute is really just a document required to register and regulate the activity of any public association, whatever its profile and purpose. For our Team, the most important thing is not the Statute but the people and the goals they pursue in sport.

We will try to set out one of the main visions behind the creation of ATTP...

So, the first and main thing is right there in the Association’s name — professional table tennis in the Republic of Moldova.

The joint work and efforts of TOP CUP Academy and SETKA-PRO over roughly 2 years have grown to an unprecedented scale, bringing together many energetic, well-meaning people who care about table tennis, who are passionate about the sport and who, through their own enthusiasm and at the cost of their time and attention, are ready to drive table tennis forward and upward.

Our goal is to make “ATTP” and “Moldovan table tennis” in general significant brands in the world of Moldovan sport.

Those inside the sport know the chaos and ambiguity currently happening in Moldovan table tennis: the lack of proper media coverage of table tennis and of our players’ achievements; almost no incentives for our champions and for those who reach international podiums under our country’s flag; the bias of the Federation’s decision-makers towards certain participants in the sporting process; a shortage of referees and, above all, a lack of advanced qualifications among those there are; too few large-scale competitions (though few people commit to organising them); a lack of funds to hold competitions (for example, this year the Federation simply was not ready to organise and hold the country’s main championship, let alone offer valuable prizes and gifts — here we truly thank our friends at TOP CUP Academy and its partners for their help and for their financial and logistical contribution). Then there is the shortage (if not absence) of sponsors; the lack of world-class performance athletes; a biased and outdated national ranking, a selective events calendar, and so on.

Until recently there were not even officially adopted Rules of table tennis in the Republic of Moldova (people were used to relying on other countries’ documents), until ATTP drafted and officially approved them.

ATTP members aim to be the people who want to change this — and who, for now, are able to.

Most visitors to TOP CUP Academy and active ATTP members have been in this sport for a long time; practising it every day, some have often travelled to international competitions, absorbing a lot of experience and useful ideas.

It is time to apply the experience of developed countries here at home, to change the situation radically. ATTP knows and understands what needs to be done and how to do it — and what it does not know, it will certainly find out. It is good that there are people of good faith who have said they want to help us.

In just two years the ATTP Team has been joined by many friends and acquaintances across the country and in neighbouring countries who are as obsessed with table tennis as we are. We need this help and support here, from people who care about table tennis.

So, for those who care about table tennis, ATTP and membership of it can be a new step in developing the pursuit they love.

After all, ATTP was also created to make the sport accessible to everyone.

Success and satisfaction in what you do and what you have!
